# Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric architecture

This page describes the Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric architecture. It explains the architectural layers and how the components work together to govern model access, tool access, and delegated identity.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

For a summary of each component, refer to [Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Architecture overview

The following diagram illustrates a travel application with agent-to-agent, model, and tool request paths, alongside catalog registration and telemetry connections. Click the diagram to view it at full size.

[![Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric architecture showing travel, booking, and
weather agents connected to the AI Inference Gateway and MCP Sidecars, model
providers, the Consul catalog, and an OpenTelemetry
collector](/img/architecture/camp-architecture.png)](/img/architecture/camp-architecture.png)

The named providers and telemetry integrations illustrate the topology rather than establish release support. Component availability and security boundaries follow the descriptions on this page and the linked component documentation.

### Architectural layers

| Layer | Responsibility | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Consul control plane | Maintain service and policy configuration and supply the resulting proxy configuration. | Does not execute agent workflows or issue user access tokens. |
| Envoy data plane | Enforce configured mesh connectivity, forward requests, and perform configured routing and retries. | Network reachability does not replace tool policy or delegated-user authorization. |
| Gateway and identity processors | Interpret supported protocols, transform payloads, and participate in policy and identity processing. | Processors operate within trusted proxy configuration rather than accepting caller-selected routes or credentials. |
| External identity and credential systems | Customer identity and access management (IAM) issues delegated tokens. Vault supplies external provider credentials. | User delegation and provider authentication remain separate trust relationships. |
| Observability and Agentic Analytics | Automatically capture supported proxy interactions, correlate operational evidence, and detect unproductive repetition. | Applications supply business outcomes; telemetry does not prove task success, and delayed analysis cannot prevent every unsafe first action. |

Consul and Envoy own mesh configuration and transport. Applications supply the workflow semantics that network components cannot infer.

## Workflows

The following workflows show how the components work together to govern model access, tool access, and delegated identity, and to observe and contain agent behavior.

### Govern model access

An application sends a supported inference request through its mesh path to the [AI Inference Gateway](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/inference-gateway). Processing before routing resolves workload identity, validates the request, and applies configured request-side data protection.

Envoy selects an eligible backend using Consul-supplied configuration. Processing after routing translates the request for that provider, normalizes supported responses, and captures usage. The external processor does not independently choose routes or run the retry loop.

The Consul catalog and service intentions decide which models are eligible. When two or more models serve a capability, Envoy fails a request over across their priority tiers. For details, refer to [Model routing and failover](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/inference-gateway#model-routing-and-failover).

### Govern tool access

The [MCP Sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/mcp-sidecar) governs Model Context Protocol (MCP) discovery and invocation. Its enforcement path combines workload identity, delegated user authority when present, and tool policy. Catalog visibility does not grant invocation permission.

When policy requires human approval, an application callback supplies a decision and a separate enforcement processor verifies evidence bound to the original action. Approval does not replace destination authorization. Backends retain ownership of tool business logic and side effects.

Approved in-mesh tool calls use configured mesh paths. External HTTP MCP calls use a terminating gateway with [external credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection). The matched route supplies a trusted credential binding, the local credential runtime supplies a usable Vault-backed credential, and the gateway verifies external TLS before forwarding.

The route and its credential must both be usable. Callers cannot select secret locations, override destination bindings, or direct a provider credential to another host.

### Delegate user identity

[On-behalf-of (OBO) delegation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity) carries user authority alongside Consul workload identity. Customer IAM remains the token issuer.

The caller-side identity processor exchanges user context for authority scoped to the next destination. The destination-side processor verifies that authority before destination policy consumes its claims. A subsequent outgoing call requires authority appropriate to the next hop, not unrestricted reuse of the previous token.

Workload TLS credentials and OAuth signing credentials have separate lifecycles. Signing material stays isolated from application configuration. Neither OBO delegation nor external credential injection defines managed-model authentication.

### Investigate operational outcomes

[AI observability](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability) connects operational signals across model and tool calls through trace correlation and model attribution. Metrics, traces, and audit evidence have distinct delivery and privacy requirements.

### Trace calls and derive metrics

The AI Inference Gateway and MCP Sidecars are the specialized proxies that [automatically instrument supported model and tool exchanges](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation). Applications do not initialize tracing SDKs or emit spans for these observations. They preserve trace context across calls so the proxy-generated evidence forms a correlated workflow trace. Aggregate this evidence into operational metrics using defined populations and time windows. Higher-order key performance indicators (KPIs) also require application-defined outcomes. Content capture remains subject to privacy and retention controls. To set it up, refer to [Configure auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation/configure-auto-instrumentation).

### Contain unproductive repetition

[Cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection) analyzes repeated workflow steps and their results. An agent repeatedly calling the same tool with the same arguments and unchanged results can produce a cycle finding. Consul uses the finding through behavior policy to open the affected agent's circuit and reject subsequent applicable requests. Analysis runs asynchronously and supplements synchronous authorization and usage controls. To set it up, refer to [Configure cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection/configure-cycle-detection).

## Shared security boundaries

- Authenticate workloads and validate delegated user authority separately. Their credentials, policies, and lifecycles are distinct.
- Keep model-provider authentication separate from OBO delegation and external credential injection.
- Bind human approval to the original action. Approval evidence does not replace destination authorization.
- Treat request identifiers as correlation values, not identities or authorization evidence.
- Treat telemetry as operational evidence, not a durable audit store or billing ledger without additional delivery and retention controls.
